market_context.summary: Saturday run — US equities and futures are closed, so every equity level here is the 2026-09-18 close (a closed session, not stale data). The index is fine and the market underneath it is not: SPY 761.69 sits 2.3% off its 150-day high and QQQ 721.45 is above both its 20- and 50-day averages, while IWM 284.10 is below both, 6.9% off its high. Underneath that, this session found NKE, LULU, LCII, THO, AZO, KBH, COST, CCL and XLU at or within 3% of 150-day lows, with JEF and CEG each down ~13% in seven sessions. One frame explains it: the 10Y at 4.94% against 3.88% effective funds is the long end pricing term premium rather than cuts, which puts utilities (XLU 41.10) on their 150-day low, keeps financials weak on credit stress, and leaves mega-cap tech holding the index up while breadth rots name by name. Crypto was bid overnight — BTC +4.0%, ETH +5.4%, SOL +5.2% — but all three sit at the top of a four-week consolidation where an honest stop is wider than the measured move, so none of them cleared. In a de-rating tape the edge is in not owning the wrong things, which is why four of today's seven ideas are exits.

recommendations.thesis: The only name I found this session that is in an uptrend rather than sitting on an extreme, and it has a dated catalyst inside the horizon. SNX closed 266.16 on 09-18, above a rising 20-day (257.66) and 50-day (254.40), 10.2% below its 150-day high of 296.47 with 79.6% of room already recovered off the low - so there is measurable structure both below the entry and above the target, which is precisely what the broken names rejected today did not have. It is outperforming SPY by 6.7 points over one month and 55.9 over six, and beating its own sector proxy XLK by 2.5 and 34.4 points on the same windows, so this is buying leadership rather than a bounce. Earnings 09-24 follow three consecutive beats of 15.97%, 41.62% and 1.69%.
recommendations.key_risk: The print is four sessions out and SNX is an IT distributor on thin single-digit gross margins, so a working-capital or demand miss re-rates it quickly - the 3m return is already -6.5% despite the strong 1m and 6m. Insiders sold 61 times for $14.4M over six months with zero open-market purchases; that is expected after a 79.6% run and is weak evidence on its own, but it is not confirmation either, and I am not claiming any.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that 296.47 is the level that has already rejected this stock once, so the target is the ceiling that defines the range rather than a breakout. That is fair, and it is why the plan trims half there instead of holding for 310. The second objection is the entry: 260 is 2.3% below Friday's close, and this report fills only 42% of its pullback entries. The answer is that 260 is not a reflex discount - it is the rising 20-day at 257.66 plus the shelf of session lows at 258.0, 258.5 and 258.8 built since 09-08. If it will not come back to its own moving average before a print, the trade does not happen, and that is an acceptable outcome. RED TEAM, kept at conviction 4 and promoted to the best-evidenced entry in this report - but the third objection is that the "positioning" evidence is half priced-in: an 82.4% analyst bullish share with no sells is a measure of consensus, not of edge, and 61 insider sales for $14.4M with zero open-market purchases points the other way. What survives as a genuine confirmation is the measured relative strength (+6.7 vs SPY and +2.5 vs XLK on one month, +55.9 and +34.4 on six), which is independent of both the technical level and the date. The score is paid for on that, not on the analyst count. The stop was also verifiably widened rather than tightened - the 1.03 ATR stop under the 09-10 low was rejected - so the 2.08:1 is not a manufactured ratio. Its 2.25 ATR stop still sits under the 2.5 ATR band where this report's stop-outs have clustered, which is the live risk on an entry that may fill days before a print.

catalyst.event: Trough-multiple balance sheet, NOT a called cycle bottom. Nothing fetched this run measures RV wholesale shipments, dealer inventory or retail registrations, so the claim is only that Thor survives the trough at 0.82x book on 0.22 debt/equity - not that the trough is in. The 2026-09-22 fiscal Q4 print is the gate on starting.
catalyst.action: WAIT. Do not buy before the 09-22 print. Start the first third only after it, and only if management does not guide to a further step down in wholesale shipments. Build the rest over the following two quarters.

recommendations.thesis: Thor trades at 0.82x its own book. Book value per share was 82.88 at the most recent quarter against a 67.77 close on 09-18, alongside 0.36x sales and 13.7x a trailing EPS of 4.96 that is itself depressed - net margin is 2.67% against a mid-cycle 5-7% for this industry, and ROE is 6.1%. The part that makes it ownable rather than merely cheap is the balance sheet: total debt to equity of 0.2185 and a current ratio of 1.707, with a 1.90% dividend covered at a 45% payout. A cyclical at a trough with almost no leverage does not need the cycle to turn quickly, it only needs to survive to the turn, and this one is being priced as if it might not. The 09-22 print is the gate on starting, not the reason to own it.
recommendations.key_risk: INVALIDATION (this thesis is wrong if): Thor guides to a further year-on-year decline in wholesale RV shipments AND net margin stays under 3% for two more consecutive quarters, OR total debt/equity rises above 0.60 from the current 0.2185, OR the dividend is cut. Any of the three removes the survive-to-the-turn premise that makes a trough multiple ownable. A falling share price alone is not invalidation - the plan already buys lower. The live risks: the RV cycle can stay at the bottom far longer than a trough multiple suggests, since these are discretionary credit-financed big-ticket purchases and a 10-year at 4.94% is the wrong backdrop for financing one. Book value is also not a floor if the downturn extends - inventory and dealer floorplan receivables are the assets being marked, and they are exactly what impairs in a prolonged slump, so 0.82x book today can become 0.82x a smaller book.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that this report is simultaneously closing LCII, an RV supplier, because Thor reports on 09-22 - so why buy the thing causing the risk. The two are consistent, and deliberately so. LCII is a stopless swing long sitting 0.6% off a 150-day low with a 138 target; the right action there is to stop owning the complex through Tuesday. THO is a different claim: accumulate the least-levered name in the same complex, after the print, over quarters, against a stated bear case rather than a stop. Neither says own the RV cycle through Tuesday morning. The second objection is that 0.82x book is cheap for a reason and the reason is the cycle. Agreed - that is what the 55 bear case prices, and it is why the entry is staged in thirds down to 58 rather than taken at once. RED TEAM, third objection and the one that moved the score: the original catalyst line claimed the "RV wholesale shipment cycle is bottoming" and no evidence item supports it. The research notes show THO was surfaced by a price/book and leverage screen and taken as "the cheapest one that can survive being wrong" - no shipment series, dealer-inventory figure or RVIA datapoint was fetched all session. Of the three evidence kinds, only the valuation anchor is a confirmation of the long: the dated catalyst is a gate, and the technical item documents a fresh 150-day low beneath two falling averages, which is evidence against the direction, not for it. Conviction cut 4 to 3 and the catalyst reworded to the claim the evidence actually makes. The thesis, the staged levels and the invalidation conditions stand - every one of them re-fetched and exact. Note also that no win_probability is stated: at 2.64:1 this idea needs better than 27.5% to break even and does not say where it beats that.

data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH RAN TO COMPLETION. notes.md carries a RESEARCH COMPLETE block at 06:26 ET plus a 06:27 addendum, so truncated is false and nothing here is reconstructed from fragments. Seven candidates were captured across eight lines (THO captured twice; the later line, which adds the explicit long_term invalidation condition, supersedes the earlier one). All seven are published — nothing was dropped at synthesis.

SATURDAY RUN, NO LIVE PRICES ANYWHERE. US equities and futures are closed. Every equity figure in this report is the 2026-09-18 close, re-fetched at synthesis and confirmed identical to the research values (finnhub, asof 2026-09-18 20:00 UTC, session=closed, age ~14.5h). That is a closed market, not stale data. All equity entries are for the next open (2026-09-21) or later.

WHY THE SHAPE IS WHAT IT IS — four exits, three entries. This was not a filter applied at synthesis; it is what the tape offered. SPY is 2.3% off its high while the research session found nine names at or within 3% of 150-day lows. In a de-rating tape a long in a broken name cannot clear 2:1 once the stop is placed honestly beyond the low it is sitting on, and four longs (AZO 0.88:1, IYR 1.71:1, SLV 0.81:1, plus JEF on unquantifiable credit risk) were rejected for exactly that. Three of the four exits close positions that were published with NO STOP — a systemic finding in its own right: five open longs (NKE, LULU, LCII, BCC, PFE) carry no stop, and the three deepest underwater are three of those five. A position nothing can demote stays in the book while it decays.

RATIOS CLUSTERED NEAR THE FLOOR — disclosed rather than explained away. Of the three ideas carrying a ratio, two sit just above their floor (MU exactly 2.00, SNX 2.08 against a 2.0 swing floor); THO is 2.64 against a 2.5 long_term floor. That clustering is the documented signature of targets fitted to clear the bar, so it is flagged here on principle. The evidence this run is the opposite, and it is in the notes: SNX's stop was set at 242.50 below the 08-24 swing low (2.25 ATR) after the NEARER stop under the 09-10 low of 253.34 was explicitly rejected at 1.03 ATR — the tighter stop would have lifted the ratio and was refused. MU's entry was held UNCHANGED at 960 rather than marked up to the 1015.80 market, which is the change that would have flattered the ratio. Both stops were re-derived at synthesis: MU 90 points = 2.09 ATR, SNX 17.50 = 2.25 ATR, both clearing the 2.0 stock floor. Both targets are prior structure (SNX 296.47 is the 150-day high; MU 1140 sits under the 1255 high), not round numbers.

FAILED SOURCES. (1) EVENT CONTRACTS ENTIRELY UNAVAILABLE — Kalshi returned 0 markets for Fed, FOMC, CPI, inflation, interest rate, recession, GDP, unemployment, oil and S&P; an empty query returned 40 rows, all multi-leg sports parlays with null yes_bid/yes_ask/last_price/volume. ZERO event contracts are published as a result — a source failure, not an absence of opportunity. Consequence: the three open event positions (KXFEDDECISION-26SEP-H25 @32, -26OCT-H25 @28, -26SEP-H0 @47) COULD NOT BE MARKED OR RESOLVED. The two 26SEP contracts reference a September FOMC that has already passed and may have resolved; they need a run with a working feed. No price was guessed. (2) NO FUTURES IDEA, because no futures or index price could be fetched — macro returned ok:false for ES, NQ, DXY, ^TNX, ^VIX, gold and WTI (Yahoo HTTP 429 on all index/FX/commodity symbols; finnhub 'market data subscription required for CFD indices'; stooq 404 on ^GSPC/^NDX/^DJI/^RUT; no Alpha Vantage key). Index context above is from ETF proxies instead, and vix/dxy/gold/wti are null rather than estimated. A contract month that cannot be priced was not named. (3) NO TRUE DAILY ATR FOR ANY CRYPTO — CoinGecko's free OHLC endpoint served 4-day bars at every window requested, so the crypto stops in the rejection notes are set below four-week structural lows rather than by ATR multiple. (4) biopharmcatalyst PDUFA calendar returned only a cookie notice and a second FDA source had no readable dates; nasdaq short-interest for UEC read-timed-out.

HORIZON SKEW IS REAL AND NOT MANUFACTURED. No intraday ideas, because the US market is closed and every level here is a Friday close — there is no intraday setup to have. Six swing and one long_term is what survived, and no idea was added or dropped for balance.
